regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Establish and maintain reasonable procedures to protect the confidentiality, security, and integrity of personal information collected from children
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operator of the District Platform used by children under 13
current_state: Children's information security program adopted 2026-03
gap_description: Support console gives 61 staff standing read access to children's records in every district tenant

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Written information security program with safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of children's information and the operator's size, complexity, and scope
current_state: Written program adopted before the 2026-04-22 compliance date
gap_description: None

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Designate one or more employees to coordinate the program
current_state: Education Software CISO designated in writing
gap_description: None

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Identify and, at least annually, assess internal and external risks to children's information and the sufficiency of safeguards
current_state: 2026 division risk analysis (P01)
gap_description: The AI tutor was launched in 2026-01 without an assessment of its risks to children's information
remediation_action: Children's privacy review gate for new features (POAM-014)

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Design, implement, and maintain safeguards based on the volume and sensitivity of children's information and the likelihood of compromise
current_state: Encryption, tenant isolation, MFA for staff
gap_description: Standing cross-tenant support access does not match the volume and sensitivity of the data (about 8 million children)

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Regularly test and monitor the effectiveness of safeguards
current_state: Annual penetration test; isolation tests each release
gap_description: No red-team or safety testing of the AI tutor (prompt injection, harmful content, data leakage)

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: At least annually evaluate and modify the program for risks, test results, and material changes
current_state: Program adopted 2026-03; first annual evaluation scheduled 2027-03-31
gap_description: None (not yet due)

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Before letting service providers or third parties collect or hold children's information, take reasonable steps to confirm their capability and obtain written assurances
current_state: Model provider contract with zero-retention and no-training terms; integration partner agreements
gap_description: 23 of about 140 integration partners have no written security assurances on file
remediation_action: Collect assurances or suspend the integrations (POAM-024)

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
requirement_summary: Retain children's information only as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose; delete it securely; never retain indefinitely
current_state: Retention policy says district data is deleted 90 days after contract end
gap_description: Data of 212 former districts is still held, some more than 3 years after contract end (scenario gap 6)
remediation_action: Delete and certify; automate end-of-contract deletion (POAM-015)

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
citation: 16 CFR 312.10 (written retention policy in the 312.4(d) notice)
requirement_summary: Maintain a written data retention policy stating purposes, business need, and deletion timeframe, and include it in the online notice
current_state: Policy published in the online notice 2026-04
gap_description: None

regulation: COPPA Rule (16 CFR Part 312, as amended 2025)
citation: 16 CFR 312.5(a)(1) (with school authorization under existing FTC guidance)
requirement_summary: Obtain verifiable parental consent before collection, use, or disclosure, including for material changes; the FTC continues to accept school authorization for use solely for the school's educational purpose under existing guidance (the 2025 amendments did not codify it)
current_state: District contracts authorize collection for the school's educational purpose
gap_description: 31 of the 140 pilot districts signed contracts before the AI tutor existed; sending children's prompts to a model provider is a material change their authorization may not cover
remediation_action: Written district authorization for the AI tutor before further use in those districts (POAM-014)
pending_rule_change: FTC said it may revisit ed tech and school authorization after ED updates FERPA rules

regulation: FERPA (as a contractor to customer institutions)
